'''Greg Anderson''' was a Players Committee [[Rules Advocate]]. In January 2002 [[Warren Holland]] named him and Joe Helfrich the first Player Advocates for Rules Support.<ref name="pc1" /> He was earlier a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Rogue 31 from Ellicott City, Md. The published fan table marks the slot Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run. At DecipherCon 1999 he finished 9th in the [[Young Jedi]] Opposites event.<ref name="dc99yj20_5">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/YJ20_5.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: YJ Opposites], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010108191900/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/YJ20_5.html Internet Archive]</ref>

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables.

== Radio Free Decipher (2002) ==
On ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' Broadcast 112 (25 January 2002), host [[Kyle Heuer]] and [[Scott Gaeta]] discussed Anderson's appointment to the first [[Players Committee]] alongside [[Joe Helfrich]] on rules. Gaeta, who knew him by reputation, called him an excellent choice.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=docK2vpQWUI&t=969s Broadcast 112 - Radio Free Decipher (25 January, 2002): Scott Gaeta on the SWCCG PC], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 16:09. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-docK2vpQWUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 112 transcript]].</ref>
